qajar-dynasty.name: Qajar dynasty
qajar-dynasty.summary: An Iranian ruling family that gained prominence in the 16th century and governed Iran from 1789 to 1925, ending when Reza Shah was declared the new shah.

persian-famine-of-1870-1872.name: Persian famine of 1870–1872
persian-famine-of-1870-1872.summary: Mass starvation and disease in Iran during the Qajar era. Explanations differ: cotton replacing grain farming, or two years of severe drought, with hoarding and market manipulation by officials and grain dealers blamed for its effects.

naser-al-din-shah-qajar.name: Naser al-Din Shah Qajar
naser-al-din-shah-qajar.summary: Fourth Shah of Qajar Iran, ruling from 1848 until his assassination in 1896; he introduced newspapers, the telegraph and photography, but his rule grew increasingly dictatorial and corrupt.

arak-drink.name: Arak
arak-drink.summary: Distilled spirit from the Levant, part of the anise drinks family.

boza.name: Boza
boza.summary: Thick, mildly alcoholic fermented drink originating in Central Asia, made from grains such as millet, wheat and maize. It is one of the oldest Turkic beverages.

mirza-al-shirazi.name: Mirza al-Shirazi
mirza-al-shirazi.summary: Iranian-Iraqi Shia leader who became the supreme Shia authority of his time after the death of Murtadha Ansari. He is famed for his 1891 verdict against tobacco use, known as the Tobacco Protest.

fatwa.name: Fatwa
fatwa.summary: Legal ruling on a point of Islamic law, given by a qualified jurist called a mufti in answer to a question. Fatwas have advised courts, taken stands on doctrine, and legitimized or protested government policies.

willem-floor.name: Willem Floor
willem-floor.summary: Dutch historian and Iranologist (born 1942) known for extensive published scholarship on the socio-economic history of Iran.

rudi-matthee.name: Rudi Matthee
rudi-matthee.summary: A historian at the University of Delaware specializing in early modern Iran, author of numerous books on Safavid and Qajar history.

qajaresque-neo-baroque-architecture.name: Qajaresque Neo-Baroque architecture
qajaresque-neo-baroque-architecture.summary: An eclectic 19th-century Persian architectural style blending traditional Persian art with Baroque Revival luxury, flourishing especially under Naser al-Din Shah Qajar and known for its use of stucco.

fath-ali-shah-at-the-hunt.name: Fath-Ali Shah at the Hunt
fath-ali-shah-at-the-hunt.summary: An oil painting of Fath-Ali Shah on a hunt, made around 1810 by the Iranian court artist Mihr 'Ali and later given to Britain as a royal gift.

mihr-ali.name: Mihr 'Ali
mihr-ali.summary: A leading royal painter of the Qajar court under Fath-Ali Shah Qajar, regarded as the most notable Iranian portraitist of the early 19th century.

mirza-baba.name: Mirza Baba
mirza-baba.summary: Iranian court painter (active c. 1785–1830) from Isfahan, one of the two most prominent Persian painters of the early 19th century.

isfahan.name: Isfahan
isfahan.summary: City in central Iran that flourished from the 9th to 18th centuries and became the Safavid capital under Abbas the Great, renowned for its Persian-Muslim architecture.

agha-mohammad-khan-qajar.name: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar
agha-mohammad-khan-qajar.summary: Founder of Iran's Qajar dynasty, ruling as Shah from 1789 to 1797; he reunified the country, made Tehran its capital, and campaigned to reassert Iranian rule over Georgia.

fath-ali-shah-qajar.name: Fath-Ali Shah Qajar
fath-ali-shah-qajar.summary: Second Shah of Qajar Iran, reigning from 1797 to 1834, whose wars with Russia cost Iran its Caucasus territories, though he also centralized the state and revived Persian arts.

kamal-ol-molk.name: Kamal-ol-molk
kamal-ol-molk.summary: An Iranian court painter, born Mohammad Ghaffari (1848–1940), whose adopted title means 'Perfection of the Realm.'

ayeneh-kari.name: Ayeneh-kari
ayeneh-kari.summary: A Persian decorative art of assembling finely cut mirrors into geometric or floral patterns to cover interior walls, prized for its shifting reflections.

gore-ouseley.name: Gore Ouseley
gore-ouseley.summary: British entrepreneur, linguist and diplomat (1770–1844) who negotiated an 1813 treaty redrawing the border between Russia and Persia.

rashtrapati-bhavan.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
rashtrapati-bhavan.summary: Official residence of the President of India in New Delhi, built 1912–1929 as the Viceroy's House and renamed after independence.

collodion-process.name: Collodion process
collodion-process.summary: An early photographic process, also called the wet-plate process, requiring material to be coated, sensitized, exposed and developed within about fifteen minutes.

gertrude-bell.name: Gertrude Bell
gertrude-bell.summary: English writer, traveller and political officer (1868–1926) who mapped the Middle East and helped shape its post-Ottoman borders and governments.

ganja-azerbaijan.name: Ganja
ganja-azerbaijan.summary: Azerbaijan's third-largest city, historically also known by the Armenian name Gandzak, and capital of the Ganja Khanate until Russia annexed it in 1813.

russo-persian-war-1804-1813.name: Russo-Persian War of 1804 to 1813
russo-persian-war-1804-1813.summary: A war between Iran and Russia over Georgia, ended in 1813 by the Treaty of Gulistan, which ceded Georgia, Dagestan and most of modern Azerbaijan to Russia.

anglo-persian-war.name: Anglo-Persian War
anglo-persian-war.summary: An 1856 to 1857 war in which Britain opposed Iran's attempt to claim the city of Herat; British forces prevailed near Bushehr and in southern Mesopotamia, and Iran withdrew from Herat.

herat.name: Herat
herat.summary: Ancient city in western Afghanistan on the Silk Road that became a major center of the Timurid Renaissance after being conquered by Timur.

sir-james-outram-1st-baronet.name: Sir James Outram
sir-james-outram-1st-baronet.summary: British army officer (1803 to 1863) who served in the conquest of Sindh and the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

bushehr.name: Bushehr
bushehr.summary: A port city in southwestern Iran, capital of Bushehr province.

treaty-of-paris-1857.name: Treaty of Paris (1857)
treaty-of-paris-1857.summary: 1857 treaty ending the Anglo-Persian War, in which Persia withdrew from Herat and gave up its territorial claims there.

treaty-of-gulistan.name: Treaty of Gulistan
treaty-of-gulistan.summary: An 1813 treaty drafted by British mediator Sir Gore Ouseley, following the Russian storming of Lankaran; it later contributed to a fresh Russo-Persian war in 1826.

great-game.name: Great Game
great-game.summary: A 19th-century rivalry between the British and Russian empires for influence in Central Asia, especially Afghanistan, Persia and Tibet, fought through diplomacy and expansion rather than direct war.

persian-cossack-brigade.name: Persian Cossack Brigade
persian-cossack-brigade.summary: A Russian-modelled cavalry unit formed in Iran in 1879, commanded by Russian officers until 1920; it later helped bring Reza Shah to power and found the Pahlavi dynasty.

krupp.name: Krupp
krupp.summary: German company that was Europe's largest at the start of the 20th century and Germany's leading weapons maker, producing battleships, tanks and artillery.

tabriz.name: Tabriz
tabriz.summary: A city in northwestern Iran and capital of East Azerbaijan province, historically also known as Tauris, noted today for its handicrafts and carpet weaving.

urmia.name: Urmia
urmia.summary: The largest city in Iran's West Azerbaijan province, near a great salt lake and the Turkish border, with a long, diverse religious history including a once-large Christian population.

khoy.name: Khoy
khoy.summary: A city in West Azerbaijan province, Iran, occupied since Median times and long an important Christian center.

abbas-mirza.name: Abbas Mirza
abbas-mirza.summary: Qajar crown prince of Iran (1789-1833) who led Iran's military campaigns against Russia and the Ottomans and pioneered the country's first reform and modernization efforts.

zamburak-iran.name: Zamburak
zamburak-iran.summary: A small cannon mounted on a camel and fired by its rider, the zamburakchi, meaning "little wasp" in Persian; used in the Iranian army from the 17th to early 20th century.

lankaran.name: Lankaran
lankaran.summary: A city in Azerbaijan on the Caspian Sea coast, near the Iranian border, with a population of about 89,300 as of 2021.

battle-of-aslanduz.name: Battle of Aslanduz
battle-of-aslanduz.summary: A battle fought on 31 October and 1 November 1812 during the Russo-Persian War, in which a smaller Russian Imperial army defeated Qajar Iran's troops and captured their spoils.

ardabil-province.name: Ardabil province
ardabil-province.summary: A province in northwestern Iran, established in 1993 and carved from East Azerbaijan province, with the city of Ardabil as its capital.

akhalkalaki.name: Akhalkalaki
akhalkalaki.summary: A town in southern Georgia on the edge of the Javakheti Plateau, with recorded history since the 11th century and a population that is mostly ethnic Armenian.

17th-horse-poona-horse.name: Poona Horse
17th-horse-poona-horse.summary: Indian Army cavalry regiment tracing back to the 3rd Bombay Light Cavalry, raised in 1820, which later fought in Persia, Afghanistan and the Indo-Pakistani wars.

ispahsalar.name: Sepahsalar
ispahsalar.summary: A title used across the Islamic world from the 10th to 15th centuries for the most senior military commander, roughly equivalent to army commander or generalissimo.

tangestan-county.name: Tangestan
tangestan-county.summary: County in Bushehr province, Iran, whose capital is the city of Ahram.

amir-kabir.name: Amir Kabir
amir-kabir.summary: Chief minister to Naser al-Din Shah Qajar, regarded as Iran's first moderniser for founding its first higher-education institution and reforming taxes and justice, before being exiled and murdered in 1852.

qaani.name: Qa'ani
qaani.summary: Pen name of Mirza Habibollah Shirazi (1808 to 1854), one of the most famous poets of Iran's Qajar era.

qasida.name: Qasida
qasida.summary: An ancient Arabic ode form using a single meter and rhyme throughout, originating in pre-Islamic poetry and later adopted into Persian and Turkish literature.

persian-constitutional-revolution.name: Persian Constitutional Revolution
persian-constitutional-revolution.summary: A 1905 to 1911 movement in Qajar Iran that established the country's first parliament, opening the way to a modern era of press debate and constitutional government.

mirza-fatali-akhundov.name: Mirza Fatali Akhundov
mirza-fatali-akhundov.summary: Azerbaijani author, playwright and literary critic (1812–1878) who wrote Europe-inspired plays, founded materialist and atheist thought in Azerbaijan, and influenced Iranian theater and nationalism.

voltaire.name: Voltaire
voltaire.summary: Pen name of French Enlightenment writer and philosopher François-Marie Arouet (1694-1778), a prolific author known for criticizing the Church and advocating freedom of speech and religion.

jalal-al-din-mirza-qajar.name: Jalal al-Din Mirza Qajar
jalal-al-din-mirza-qajar.summary: Iranian historian, philologist and freethinker (1827-1872) who wrote Name-ye Khosrovan, a semi-historical work on Iran's history and possibly the first major nationalistic account of the country.

mirza-aqa-khan-kermani.name: Mirza Aqa Khan Kermani
mirza-aqa-khan-kermani.summary: Iranian intellectual reformer and literary critic (1854–1896/97) whose calls for political and social change helped set the stage for Iran's Constitutional Revolution of 1906.

mirza-malkam-khan.name: Mirza Malkam Khan
mirza-malkam-khan.summary: Iranian modernist writer, diplomat and publicist (1834–1908), the first Christian to hold the title 'Mirza', considered a father of the Iranian Constitutional Revolution.

neshat-esfahani.name: Neshat Esfahani
neshat-esfahani.summary: An Iranian official and poet (1759–1829) who wielded great political influence under Qajar shah Fath-Ali Shah, serving as first foreign minister and later de facto prime minister.

bazgasht-e-adabi.name: Bazgasht-e adabi
bazgasht-e-adabi.summary: An 18th-century Iranian literary movement, meaning 'Literary Return', that called for reviving older Khorasani and Iraqi styles of Persian poetry.

saadi-shirazi.name: Saadi Shirazi
saadi-shirazi.summary: A 13th-century Persian Sufi poet (1209/10–1291/92), regarded as one of the greatest of the classical Persian tradition and nicknamed "the Master of Speech."

gulistan-book.name: Gulistan
gulistan-book.summary: A landmark 1258 work of Persian prose by the poet Saadi Shirazi, a collection of poems and stories offering moral and practical advice, including guidance for rulers.

mirza-jahangir-khan.name: Mirza Jahangir Khan
mirza-jahangir-khan.summary: Iranian writer and revolutionary (c. 1870/75–1908) who founded the satirical newspaper Sur-e Esrafil and was executed for his role in the Constitutional Revolution.

mohammad-farrokhi-yazdi.name: Farrokhi Yazdi
mohammad-farrokhi-yazdi.summary: Iranian poet, journalist and senior politician (1889–1939) known as the "Crown of poets," active during the Persian Constitutional Revolution and the Reza Pahlavi era.

balochi-language.name: Balochi language
balochi-language.summary: A Northwestern Iranian language spoken by about 8.8 million Baloch people across Pakistan, Iran, Afghanistan and beyond, with a literary tradition dating from the early 19th century.

balochistan.name: Balochistan
balochistan.summary: A historical, arid region of desert and mountains split among Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan, populated mainly by ethnic Baloch and strategically important for its coastline and mineral wealth.

gorani-language.name: Gurani
gorani-language.summary: A Northwestern Iranian language or group of dialects spoken in small pockets of Iraq and Iran, whose main dialect, Hawrami, was once a literary language for Kurds.

mastoureh-ardalan.name: Mastoureh Ardalan
mastoureh-ardalan.summary: An Iranian Kurdish poet, historian, and writer (1805 to 1848) who wrote mainly in Persian and Gorani.

sanandaj.name: Sanandaj
sanandaj.summary: Capital of Iran's Kurdistan province, a historic centre of Kurdish culture known for its music, poetry and carpet weaving, called Senna in Kurdish.

raffi-novelist.name: Raffi
raffi-novelist.summary: Armenian author (1835–1888) and leading 19th-century literary figure whose historical novels helped shape modern Armenian nationalism.

george-iii.name: George III
george-iii.summary: King of Great Britain and Ireland from 1760 to 1820, whose reign saw victory over France in the Seven Years' War but the loss of Britain's American colonies.

joseph-cochran.name: Joseph Cochran
joseph-cochran.summary: American Presbyterian missionary and doctor credited with founding Iran's first modern Western medical school, in Urmia in 1879.

urmia-university.name: Urmia University
urmia-university.summary: A public university near Urmia in Iran with six campuses and over 14,000 students, ranked among Iran's top-tier institutions.

adolf-fonahn.name: Adolf Fonahn
adolf-fonahn.summary: Norwegian physician and medical historian (1873–1940) who studied Persian and Arabic medical literature, Tibetan Buddhism, and Leonardo da Vinci's anatomical drawings.

avicenna.name: Avicenna (Ibn Sina)
avicenna.summary: Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), known in the West as Avicenna, was a leading philosopher and physician of the Islamic Golden Age whose Canon of Medicine remained a standard European medical text until 1650.

zand-dynasty.name: Zand dynasty
zand-dynasty.summary: An Iranian dynasty founded by Karim Khan Zand of the Zand tribe of the Laks, who ruled Iran from 1751 to 1779.

afsharid-dynasty.name: Afsharid dynasty
afsharid-dynasty.summary: An Iranian dynasty founded by Nader Shah, who ruled 1736 to 1747, drawn from the Turkoman Afshar tribe, governing Afsharid Iran.

guarded-domains-of-iran.name: Guarded Domains of Iran
guarded-domains-of-iran.summary: The official name of Iran from the Safavid era until the early 20th century, reflecting a shared sense of territorial and cultural unity.

tobacco-protest.name: Tobacco Protest
tobacco-protest.summary: A mass protest in Qajar Iran against an 1890 British monopoly over the country's tobacco trade, climaxing in a widely obeyed 1891 fatwa banning tobacco use.

shusha.name: Shusha
shusha.summary: City in the Karabakh mountains that became capital of the Karabakh Khanate founded by Panah Ali Khan in the 1750s, and later a cultural center of the South Caucasus.

south-caucasus.name: Transcaucasia
south-caucasus.summary: Also called the South Caucasus, a region on the southern Caucasus Mountains roughly matching modern Armenia, Georgia and Azerbaijan.

dagestan.name: Dagestan
dagestan.summary: A republic of Russia in the North Caucasus along the Caspian Sea, sharing borders with Azerbaijan, Georgia and several Russian republics; one of Russia's most ethnically and linguistically diverse regions.

treaty-of-turkmenchay.name: Treaty of Turkmenchay
treaty-of-turkmenchay.summary: 1828 treaty ending the Russo-Persian War of 1826 to 1828, forcing Qajar Iran to cede the Erivan, Nakhchivan and Talysh khanates in the South Caucasus to Russia.

national-consultative-assembly.name: Majles (National Consultative Assembly)
national-consultative-assembly.summary: Iran's national legislative body from 1906 to 1979, established by the Persian Constitution of 1906 and elected by universal suffrage, later including women after 1963.

d-arcy-concession.name: D'Arcy Concession
d-arcy-concession.summary: An 1901 agreement giving William Knox D'Arcy exclusive rights to prospect for oil in Persia; after early setbacks it led to a major strike in 1908 and was cancelled in 1932.

mohammad-ali-shah-qajar.name: Mohammad Ali Shah Qajar
mohammad-ali-shah-qajar.summary: Sixth shah of the Qajar dynasty, ruling Iran from 1907 until being deposed in 1909; grandson of the early moderniser Amir Kabir through his mother.

mohammad-shah-qajar.name: Mohammad Shah Qajar
mohammad-shah-qajar.summary: Third Qajar shah of Iran, ruling from 1834 to 1848; his reign included a failed 1837 siege of Herat and the suppression of rival claimants and revolts.

faramosh-khaneh.name: Faramosh Khaneh
faramosh-khaneh.summary: An influential secret society in 19th-century Iran, modeled on Masonic lodges and founded by Mirza Malkam Khan, spreading liberal ideas drawn from the French Revolution.

ministry-of-information-and-communicatio.name: Ministry of Post and Telegraph
ministry-of-information-and-communicatio.summary: Iran's government ministry, established in 1908, responsible for postal services, telephones and information technology.
ministry-of-information-and-communicatio.source_title: Ministry of Information and Communications Technology of Iran

yousuf-khan-mostashar-al-dowleh.name: Mostashar al-Dowleh
yousuf-khan-mostashar-al-dowleh.summary: An Iranian writer, intellectual and diplomat (1823–1895) known for a secular treatise and for spreading liberal ideas in Qajar-era Iran.

abol-qasem-qa-em-maqam.name: Abol-Qasem Qa'em-Maqam
abol-qasem-qa-em-maqam.summary: Iranian official and prose writer (1779–1835) who served as grand vizier under Qajar king Mohammad Shah and helped negotiate treaties with the Ottomans and Russians.

amir-aslan-khan-majd-od-dowleh.name: Amir-Aslan Khan Majd od-Dowleh
amir-aslan-khan-majd-od-dowleh.summary: A Qajar prince, statesman and court official who died in 1909, son of Mohammad-Qasem Khan Amirsoleimani and brother of Malek Jahan Khanom.

mozaffar-ad-din-shah-qajar.name: Mozaffar ad-Din Shah Qajar
mozaffar-ad-din-shah-qajar.summary: Fifth Qajar shah of Iran, reigning 1896–1907, credited with approving Iran's first constitution shortly before his death.

iranian-enlightenment.name: Iranian Enlightenment
iranian-enlightenment.summary: A movement that brought new ideas into traditional Iranian society from the mid-19th to early 20th centuries, spurred by cultural exchange after Iran's defeat in the Russo-Persian War of 1826-1828.

russo-persian-war-1826-1828.name: Russo-Persian War of 1826 to 1828
russo-persian-war-1826-1828.summary: The last major war between Russia and Qajar Iran over the South Caucasus, ending in 1828 with the Treaty of Turkmenchay, which stripped Iran of its remaining Caucasus territories.

qajar-iran.name: Qajar Iran
qajar-iran.summary: The Iranian state ruled by the Qajar dynasty from 1789 to 1925, founded by Agha Mohammad Khan, which faced major challenges to its sovereignty from Russia and Britain during the Great Game.

circassians.name: Circassians
circassians.summary: A Northwest Caucasian ethnic group native to Circassia, mostly Muslim, who were exiled and scattered after the 19th-century Russo-Circassian War and Circassian genocide.

zanj.name: Zanj
zanj.summary: A medieval term used by Muslim geographers for the Swahili Coast of Southeast Africa and its Bantu inhabitants; source of the name Zanzibar.

ayrums.name: Ayrums
ayrums.summary: A Turkic tribal group historically linked to the area around Gyumri, later regarded as a sub-ethnic group of Azerbaijanis.

karapapakhs.name: Karapapakhs
karapapakhs.summary: A Turkic people who settled along the Debed river in eastern Georgia before moving to Iran and the Ottoman Empire after 1828, later assimilated by Azerbaijanis and deported to Central Asia in 1944.

lezgins.name: Lezgins
lezgins.summary: A Northeast Caucasian ethnic group native to southern Dagestan and northern Azerbaijan, with an egalitarian, clan-based society and a traditional code of honour called Lezgiwal.

bandar-abbas-vishnu-temple.name: Bandar Abbas Vishnu Temple
bandar-abbas-vishnu-temple.summary: A monument in Bandar Abbas, Iran, built in 1892 and dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu by the Indian community working for the British East India Company.

arya-samaj.name: Arya Samaj
arya-samaj.summary: A monotheistic Hindu reform movement founded in the 1870s by Dayananda Saraswati, the first Hindu organization to actively seek converts.

krishna.name: Krishna
krishna.summary: Major Hindu deity worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu, revered for love, compassion and protection; a central figure in the Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita.
